issues.text: The gloss overstates both APIs. DbCommand.ExecuteScalar docs (net-10.0): "Executes the command and returns the first column of the first row in the first returned result set. All other columns, rows and result sets are ignored." It neither requires nor checks that the query produces a single value. ExecuteNonQuery is not defined by producing nothing either - it runs the statement and returns the number of rows affected. True of the two to_regclass queries here, but written as the general contract, and not in the claims ledger (claim 10 covers only the NULL -> DBNull mapping).
issues.fix: Reword to the documented behaviour without new vocabulary: "`ExecuteScalar` runs a query and hands back the first value in its result; `ExecuteNonQuery` runs SQL whose result is not read back." If the sentence stays as it is, add a claim to .meta.json (kind fact, version_key dotnet, section 5) covering the ExecuteScalar/ExecuteNonQuery contract.
issues.quote: `ExecuteScalar` runs a query and hands back the single value it produces; `ExecuteNonQuery` runs SQL that produces none.

issues.text: `scripts/up.sh` does not name the container. At stage-1 it runs ./scripts/dev-secrets.sh, a flutter build web, then `docker compose up -d --build --wait`; the name comes from docker-compose.yml, whose db: service sets `container_name: donhang-db`. This sentence is the reader's only anchor for a name they have to type, so pointing at the wrong file costs them the one place they could check it.
